covers: Wall Street to about 14:15 New York time (21:15 SAST) and global markets on Tuesday 3 November 2026, building on the 18:20 evening update
headline: Brent slides towards a four-week low near $103 on peace-talk hopes; Nasdaq holds a 1% gain into the afternoon as US votes; Meta taps bond market for up to $25 billion
summary: Brent was down about 1% at $103.44 a barrel at 20:18 SAST, heading for its lowest close since 7 October as traders weighed Ukraine and Iran peace talks (Reuters via Khaleej Times, 3 Nov). On Wall Street the Nasdaq was up 1.02% and the S&P 500 up 0.55% at about 21:07 SAST, the Dow down 0.25%, and the 10-year Treasury yield up 5.6 basis points to 4.95%, with AMD results due after the close and midterm results overnight (Yahoo Finance, 3 Nov). In South Africa the rand was at R16.64/$ in the afternoon, about 0.3% weaker, ahead of Wednesday's local elections, when the JSE is closed (CNBC Africa/Reuters, 3 Nov).

items.title: Brent heads for its lowest close since 7 October, near $103.44, as peace talks weigh
items.summary: At 13:18 New York time (20:18 SAST) Brent was down $1.33, about 1%, at $103.44 a barrel and WTI down $0.56 at $95.90, putting Brent on track for its lowest close since 7 October and WTI for its lowest since 14 October (Reuters via Khaleej Times, 3 Nov). Traders are weighing talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against supply risks from recent attacks; a senior Iranian official said the two sides remain far from a deal, and ING said it is probably too early to assume escalation risks have passed. Earlier, Brent swung between $107.24 and $100.80 (OilPrice.com, 3 Nov). Lower oil helps the rand and SA fuel prices but weighs on Sasol.

items.title: US job openings 7.5 million in September, above the ~7.13 million expected; quits rise to 3.4 million
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said openings were 'little changed at 7.5 million', hires 5.4 million (3.4% rate) and quits rose to 3.4 million (released 17:00 SAST, 3 Nov). Schwab's preview had expected about 7.13 million openings and 3.05 million quits. A firmer labour market lowers the odds of quick Fed cuts; the October jobs report follows on Friday.
items.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, 3 Nov 2026; Charles Schwab, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Nasdaq +1.02%, S&P 500 +0.55%, Dow −0.25% at 14:07 New York time; 10-year yield 4.95%
items.summary: At about 14:07 New York time (21:07 SAST) the Nasdaq was at 25,421.95 (+1.02%), the S&P 500 at 7,582.64 (+0.55%) and the Dow at 51,852.94 (−0.25%), little changed from the morning as chip stocks led and Apple weighed on the Dow. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 5.6 basis points to 4.95% after strong job openings data. Bitcoin fell more than 3% to near $77,600 by midday New York time as more than $1 billion left US bitcoin funds over two days after the Binance hack (Yahoo Finance, 3 Nov).

items.title: Midday: Shopify −6.3%, Palantir −2.8%, Apple −2.2% after results; CrowdStrike buys two AI security start-ups
items.summary: At 12:01 New York time Shopify was down 6.27%, Palantir 2.83% and Apple 2.15%, well off their pre-market lows (StockTitan, 3 Nov). CrowdStrike agreed to buy two AI security start-ups for a combined $495 million and its shares rose more than 2% early (Yahoo Finance, 3 Nov).

items.title: Nasdaq-100 enters its third correction of the year on AI spending worries
items.summary: The Nasdaq-100 fell 1.39% on Monday 2 November to close at 27,989, about 10.4% below its record high of 6 October (near 31,400), putting it in a technical correction (a fall of 10% or more) for the third time in 2026. Worries about the returns on heavy AI spending after the big-tech results are the main driver (XTB, 3 Nov; Bloomberg, 2 Nov).

items.title: November fuel prices: diesel down R1.10–R1.20 a litre, petrol down only 1c from Wednesday
items.summary: From 00:01 on Wednesday 4 November, 93 and 95 petrol fall 1c a litre, diesel 0.05% falls R1.10 and diesel 0.005% R1.20, while illuminating paraffin (wholesale) rises R2.75 a litre and LPGas R1.83/kg, per the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources. The general fuel levy cut (R1.50/l petrol, R3/l diesel) is partly offset by a new slate levy of 135.84c/l. Cheaper diesel helps transport, farming and mining costs (Stuff, 3 Nov).

items.title: US letter gives 60 days' notice: SA's AGOA status to end on 1 January 2027
items.summary: BusinessTech reports that President Trump wrote to President Ramaphosa giving 60 days' notice that South Africa's AGOA trade beneficiary status will end on 1 January 2027, citing slow progress on corruption and trade barriers, and foreign policy concerns. Exporters of vehicles, citrus and other farm goods are the most exposed. On Monday the rand gained about 0.4% to R16.64/$ and traded at R16.62/$ on Tuesday morning; the Top-40 rose about 1% and the 2035 bond yield fell 2.5 basis points to 8.565%. NAAMSA new vehicle sales rose 10.4% year on year in October.

items.title: Rand at R16.64/$, about 0.3% weaker; Top 40 down about 0.7%; 2035 yield 8.52%
items.summary: At 15:04 SAST the rand traded at 16.6425 per dollar, about 0.3% down from its previous close, as investors weighed the end of AGOA access and waited for Wednesday's local elections. The Top 40 was down about 0.7% and the 2035 government bond yield fell 1.5 basis points to 8.52%. The JSE is closed on Wednesday.

items.title: JSE gold and PGM miners bounce 3–6% on Monday; Sasol falls 5.6% with oil
items.summary: On Monday 2 November Gold Fields rose 5.9% to R585.50, Implats 4.5% to R171.20, Harmony 4.1% to R255.70, AngloGold Ashanti 3.9% to R1,392 and Sibanye-Stillwater 3.3% to R36.96, recovering part of Friday's 5.6%–6.4% falls, while Sasol fell 5.6% to R273.20 as oil slumped (LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026).

Traders are weighing talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against supply risks from recent attacks; a senior Iranian official said the two sides remain far from a deal, and ING said it is probably too early to assume escalation risks have passed. items.title: Gold slips about 1% to near $3,907 as the US votes
items.summary: Spot gold fell 1% to $3,906.71 an ounce during Tuesday trading (TokenPost, 3 Nov), after easing 0.5% to $3,926 earlier (Reuters, 3 Nov). Friday's one-year low was about $3,870.

items.title: Australia raises rates to 4.85% (earlier Tuesday), citing fuel-driven inflation
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85% from 4.60% at 05:30 SAST on Tuesday, its fifth increase this year and the highest level since November 2008; six board members voted to raise and three to hold (Domain; investingLive, 3 Nov). The bank said inflation will stay above target for longer than forecast, partly because of higher global fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict, and does not expect it back in its 2–3% band until late 2027 (Domain, 3 Nov). Governor Michele Bullock gave no guidance on the next move, and the Australian dollar eased after the widely expected decision (investingLive, 3 Nov). It is another sign that oil-driven inflation is keeping central banks cautious, which matters for the SARB's next steps and for the rand.

items.title: AMD (LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, target $641.00) up about 4.8% ahead of results after the US close tonight
items.summary: AMD was up 4.80% in afternoon New York trading (Yahoo Finance, 3 Nov), after rising more than 3% before the open (CNBC via StockTitan). The LRC Stock Scanner's 18:45 SAST run shows AMD at HOLD with a target of $641.00 (it showed SELL, target $402.73, in the previous edition). Results and guidance after 23:00 SAST will show whether the chip rally holds. The rating is not changed here.
items.source: Yahoo Finance, 3 Nov 2026; StockTitan, 3 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Meta (LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, target $547.40) markets a $20–25 billion bond sale for AI build-out; shares up 2.4%
items.summary: Meta is reportedly targeting $20 billion to $25 billion from a five-part US dollar investment-grade bond sale to fund AI infrastructure (MT Newswires via MarketScreener, 3 Nov). The shares were at $621.29 at 14:17 New York time, up 2.40% from $606.73. It follows a $25 billion bond sale in April, after Meta raised its 2026 capex forecast to $125–145 billion (MarketScreener, 30 Apr). The share price is already above the scanner's target; heavier borrowing for AI is the key question for the rating. Rating unchanged.
items.source: MarketScreener (MT Newswires), 3 Nov 2026; MarketScreener, 30 Apr 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Palantir (LRC Stock Scanner: BUY, target $230.00): revenue up 96% but contract signings slow; shares −2.8% at midday
items.summary: Q3 revenue was $2.31 billion (+96% year on year, versus about $2.18 billion expected) and adjusted EPS $0.44 versus $0.41, but total contract value grew only 6% to $2.918 billion, from 49% in Q2 (Tradingpedia, 3 Nov). Shares fell 6% before the open and were down 2.83% at 12:01 New York time (StockTitan, 3 Nov). The scanner's 18:45 SAST run shows Palantir at BUY with a $230.00 target; Apple is HOLD, target $227.90. Ratings are not changed here.
items.source: Tradingpedia, 3 Nov 2026; StockTitan, 3 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Lumentum closes 18.6% lower and Marvell 12.7% lower after their $115 billion all-stock deal
items.summary: Lumentum fell 18.59% to $684.40 and Marvell 12.72% to $171.41 on Monday (StockTitan, 2 Nov) after Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share (Marvell press release, 2 Nov). Because the price is fixed in Marvell shares, Marvell's fall cuts the deal's value to Lumentum holders. LRC Stock Scanner (2 Nov): Lumentum HOLD, score 52; Marvell HOLD, score 59, with a short-side trigger level of $206.50 — ratings unchanged.
items.source: StockTitan, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026
